# Status

Every countable fact this repo states about itself, measured from the
tree. **Generated by `tools/status.py`; do not edit by hand.** No
other document quotes these numbers -- they link here, because a
number written twice is a number that will disagree with itself.

`python3 tools/verify_all.py` checks that this file still matches the
tree, so a change that moves a number and does not regenerate fails.

than a measurement. What each directory is for is in

doing next is in [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md); what each check uniquely sees
is in `tools/verify_all.py`, beside the command that runs it.

## Ratchets

A ratchet is a violation the architecture has not reached yet: a count
that may fall and may never rise, tied to the step of
[`PLAYER_ARCHITECTURE.md`](PLAYER_ARCHITECTURE.md#order-of-work) that
clears it. **Raising one is a change to that document, not a line edit
in a checker**, and there is deliberately no suppression comment.

| Ratchet | Where | Now | Baseline |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `uncited-exports` | `tools/verify_port.py` | 81 | 81 |

All 14 rules in `verify_layers.py` are `error` at zero;
a new violation of any of them fails the build rather than moving
a number. `uncited-exports` above is the only ratchet in the repo:
every exported function in `game/` should cite the exe function it
ports or declare itself `[port-only]`.

## The checks

Authored in `tools/verify_all.py` and rendered here, so there is one
list and not five. `python3 tools/verify_all.py` runs them all and
reports pass, fail and **skip** separately -- a check that asserted
nothing exits 3 and is never counted as green.

24 of them need the installed game and 25 need an exported
bundle. **That is a known hole, not a design:** a machine with
neither cannot run the checks that compare two histories, and a
bundle-free fixture is the open work that closes it.
